midnight-ink.$description: Midnight Ink — Primary text, filled pill buttons, hairline borders, dark surfaces — the only chromatic color in the system; near-black with a barely-perceptible cool navy cast that softens the contrast against warm cream without losing the gravitas of pure black

warm-parchment.$description: Warm Parchment — Page canvas and light surface base — a creamy off-white that replaces the default SaaS pure-white with paper warmth, making the page feel printed rather than rendered

soft-linen.$description: Soft Linen — Elevated card and panel surface — one step darker than the canvas, used sparingly to lift a card or a section band without introducing a new color

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — SVG icon fills and decorative monochrome marks — reserved for vector assets where true black reads cleaner than the navy-tinted Midnight Ink

blush-coral.$description: Blush Coral — Sporadic warm accent — emerges from the hero aurora and may surface in tag dots or decorative washes; the only warm hue that earns a place in an otherwise cool-neutral system

zjsansdisplay.$description: Primary typeface for body, navigation, subheadings, and the 40–48px heading range. The 12px eyebrow and tag text carries +0.05em tracking (letter-spacing: 0.6px at 12px) to read as a small caps eyebrow; everything at 16px and above sits at -0.02em (-0.32px at 16px) for tight, editorial density. This is the working sans that does 95% of the page's communicative labor.

featuredecklight.$description: Hero display face used at 60–90px with line-height compressed to 1.07–1.11. Weight 100 is the anti-convention signature: while every agency site uses 600–800 for display, this hairline weight makes the largest text the lightest on the page — authority through restraint, not volume. The italic cut is used for poetic emphasis words inside the headline (e.g. 'the world').
